title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: Suppose that \(S\) is a finite set of positive integers. If the greatest integer in \(S\) is removed from \(S,\) then the average value (arithmetic mean) of the integers remaining is \(32.\) If the least integer in \(S\) is also removed, then the average value of the integers remaining is \(35.\) If the greatest integer is then returned to the set, the average value of the integers rises to \(40.\) The greatest integer in the original set \(S\) is \(72\) greater than the least integer in \(S.\) What is the average value of all the integers in the set \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(n=|S|,\) let \(T\) be the total, \(M\) the greatest, and \(L\) the least. Then \(\dfrac{T-M}{n-1}=32,\) \(\dfrac{T-M-L}{n-2}=35,\) and \(\dfrac{T-L}{n-1}=40.\)

Subtracting the first from the third: \(\dfrac{M-L}{n-1}=8.\) Since \(M-L=72,\) we get \(n-1=9,\) so \(n=10.\)

Then \(T-M=288\) and \(T-L=360.\) The middle equation gives \(T-M-L=35\cdot 8=280,\) so \(L=288-280=8\) and \(M=80.\)

Thus \(T=288+80=368,\) and the average is \(\dfrac{368}{10}=36.8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(n=|S|,\) total \(T,\) greatest \(M,\) least \(L;\) write each average as an equation
